actor: Federal district judge presiding over AI-search copyright complaint
job: Rule on motion-to-dismiss in an AI-search-vs-publisher copyright case so an appellate-grade signal can form on AI-search copyright doctrine.
outcome: A reasoned MTD order that either narrows or sustains the publisher copyright theory against an AI search engine, becoming the federal anchor.
motivation: Docket pressure from nine active publisher suits against one AI search vendor forces an early dispositive ruling to channel parallel litigation.

task.what: Issue motion-to-dismiss ruling on copyright theory
task.where: Southern District of New York docket
task.when: Briefing and decision runway through H1 2027
task.how: Reasoned written order on dispositive motion

actor: Plaintiff publisher general counsel in AI-search copyright suits

outcome: A live federal copyright case posture ripe enough that the court must rule on the motion to dismiss inside the H1 2027 window.
motivation: Publisher revenue depends on establishing licensing-rate benchmarks before AI-search traffic substitution erodes the underlying advertising and subscription base.

task.what: File amended complaints and discovery briefs
task.when: Pleading and discovery runway 2026 to H1 2027

outcome: A first named enforcement action against a general-purpose AI provider that establishes the EU front of the three-front regulatory contour.
motivation: The August 2 2026 full-enforceability deadline requires a visible first action to credibly anchor the Code as enforceable rather than voluntary.

task.what: Open and prosecute first GPAI enforcement action
task.where: EU AI Office under the AI Act
task.how: Investigation, finding, and published enforcement decision

actor: DOJ Office of Legal Policy preemption lawyer

outcome: A filed DOJ amicus brief opposing a state AI-labor-disclosure statute that lands inside H1 2027 and seeds the state-preemption front.
motivation: Successor state statutes after Colorado SB 26-189 risk fragmenting AI labor-disclosure rules in ways that conflict with federal labor and AI policy posture.

task.who: DOJ Office of Legal Policy lawyer
